```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
library(prolfqua)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Purpose

This article fits every modelling method of `build_contrast_analysis()` to one simulated experiment and compares their results with `ContrastsComparison`:

- which protein and contrast pairs each method estimates
- how closely the methods' estimates agree on the pairs they share
- which pairs each method calls significant, and where the methods contradict each other
- how the results of another tool are compared, here plain limma

What each method models is described in the vignette [All modelling methods at a glance](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/articles/ModellingMethods.html). How the methods perform on data with known changes is measured in [prolfquabenchmark](https://prolfqua.github.io/prolfquabenchmark/vignettes/Benchmark_results.html).

# Simulate one experiment

```{r simulate}
sim <- sim_lfq_data_peptide_config(n_proteins = 80, seed = 42)
lfq_peptide <- LFQData$new(sim$data, sim$config)
lfq_peptide <- lfq_peptide$get_Transformer()$log2()$lfq
lfq_protein <- lfq_peptide$get_Aggregator()$aggregate()
lfq_limpa <- AggregateLimpa$new(lfq_peptide, "protein")$aggregate()
contrasts <- c(A_vs_Ctrl = "group_A - group_Ctrl", B_vs_Ctrl = "group_B - group_Ctrl")

peptides <- lfq_peptide$data_long()
peptides_per_protein <- dplyr::count(dplyr::distinct(peptides, protein_Id, peptide_Id), protein_Id)
```

The experiment has `r nrow(peptides_per_protein)` proteins with `r sum(peptides_per_protein$n)` peptides in `r length(unique(peptides$sampleName))` samples of three groups. `r round(100 * mean(is.na(peptides[[lfq_peptide$response()]])))` % of the peptide intensities are missing, and `r sum(peptides_per_protein$n == 1)` proteins have a single peptide. The peptides are aggregated to proteins by median polish (`lfq_protein`), and for `limpa` by limpa's detection probability model (`lfq_limpa`), which also gives each protein intensity a standard error.

# Fit every method

`list_facades()` lists the methods. Each declares the input it needs: `aggregated` methods take the proteins, `nested` methods take the peptides and report protein contrasts. Every method models the group; `lmer_nested` adds random effects for peptide and sample. The families group the methods as in the factory figure of the README.

```{r fit, warning = FALSE}
facades <- Filter(function(facade) facade$package == "prolfqua", list_facades())
styles <- utils::read.delim(system.file("extdata", "facade_styles.tsv", package = "prolfqua"))
methods <- intersect(styles$method, names(facades))
family <- stats::setNames(styles$family, styles$method)[methods]

input_for <- function(method) {
  if (method == "limpa") {
    return(lfq_limpa)
  }
  if (facades[[method]]$needs == "nested") lfq_peptide else lfq_protein
}
model_for <- function(method) {
  if (method == "lmer_nested") "~ group_ + (1 | peptide_Id) + (1 | sampleName)" else "~ group_"
}
analyses <- lapply(stats::setNames(methods, methods), function(method) {
  build_contrast_analysis(input_for(method), model_for(method), contrasts, method = method)
})
```

```{r methods_table}
data.frame(
  method = methods,
  family = family,
  input = vapply(facades[methods], function(facade) facade$needs, character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, caption = "The methods, their family and the input they take.")
```

# Align the results

`ContrastsComparison` reads the effect, statistic, p-value and FDR of every method through its `ContrastConfiguration` and aligns the methods on protein and contrast. `$aligned()` has one row per pair and method, over all pairs that any method reports. The `status` of a pair in a method is `not estimated` (no row, or no effect), `not tested` (an effect without an FDR), `not significant`, or `up` and `down` (FDR below the threshold, here 0.1).

```{r align}
comparison <- ContrastsComparison$new(analyses, fdr_threshold = 0.1)
aligned <- comparison$aligned()
aligned$family <- family[aligned$method]
n_pairs <- nrow(dplyr::distinct(aligned, protein_Id, contrast))
head(aligned, 3)
```

```{r status, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9, fig.cap = paste0("Status of the ", n_pairs, " protein and contrast pairs in each method, both contrasts, FDR threshold 0.1. Methods grouped by family. not estimated: the method reports no effect for the pair; not tested: an effect without a p-value.")}
status_colours <- c(
  up = "#b2182b",
  down = "#2166ac",
  `not significant` = "grey75",
  `not tested` = "grey90",
  `not estimated` = "#e6ab02"
)
aligned |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    method = factor(method, levels = rev(methods)),
    family = factor(family, levels = unique(styles$family)),
    status = factor(status, levels = names(status_colours))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = method, fill = status)) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_grid(family ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colours) +
  labs(x = "protein and contrast pairs", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
```

# Which pairs each method estimates

`$coverage()` counts the pairs per set of methods that estimate them. The table names the methods missing from each set.

```{r coverage}
comparison$coverage() |>
  dplyr::mutate(not_estimated_by = vapply(
    strsplit(estimated_by, " & ", fixed = TRUE),
    function(by) toString(setdiff(methods, by)),
    character(1)
  )) |>
  dplyr::mutate(not_estimated_by = dplyr::if_else(not_estimated_by == "", "(none)", not_estimated_by)) |>
  dplyr::select(not_estimated_by, pairs) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Protein and contrast pairs, by the methods that do not estimate them.")
```

```{r upset, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 10, warning = FALSE, fig.cap = "UpSet plot of the protein and contrast pairs each method estimates. Bars on top: pairs estimated by exactly the methods marked below them."}
comparison$upset()
```

`lmer_nested` does not estimate the `r sum(peptides_per_protein$n == 1)` proteins with a single peptide: its random peptide effect needs at least two peptides. `$provenance()` records them:

```{r provenance_lmer}
analyses$lmer_nested$provenance()
```

```{r gap}
gap <- aligned |>
  dplyr::filter(method == "lm", status == "not estimated") |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast)
```

`lm` and the other methods that model only the observed intensities do not estimate `r nrow(gap)` pairs, because their proteins have no observation in a group:

```{r gap_intensities}
lfq_protein$data_long() |>
  dplyr::filter(protein_Id %in% gap$protein_Id) |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, sampleName, intensity = dplyr::all_of(lfq_protein$response())) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sampleName, values_from = intensity) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Per-sample protein intensities (log2, median polish) of the proteins that lm cannot estimate.")
```

The `_impute` methods estimate these pairs with the missing group at the limit of detection, `limpa` and `limpa_nested` with their detection probability model, and the detection models from the detection pattern; their estimates are listed with the conflicts below.

# The pairs of one method

`$pairs()` returns the pairs of one method that have all the given columns. The detection model `binomial_firth_nested` estimates an effect for every pair but a p-value only for some: a protein whose peptides are detected in every sample has no difference in detection to test.

```{r pairs}
c(
  effect = nrow(comparison$pairs("binomial_firth_nested", columns = "effect")),
  effect_and_p_value = nrow(comparison$pairs("binomial_firth_nested", columns = c("effect", "p.value")))
)
```

The pairs that several methods share are the intersection of their `$pairs()`. The detection models estimate log odds of detection; the other methods estimate log2 fold changes of intensity. Their estimates are compared on the pairs that all intensity methods estimate:

```{r shared}
intensity <- methods[family != "detection"]
shared <- Reduce(dplyr::intersect, lapply(intensity, function(method) comparison$pairs(method)))
estimates <- aligned |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% intensity) |>
  dplyr::semi_join(shared, by = c("protein_Id", "contrast"))
nrow(shared)
```

# Estimates on the same pairs

```{r effect_vs_lm, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 9, fig.cap = paste0("Log2 fold change of each intensity method against lm, on the ", nrow(shared), " protein and contrast pairs that all intensity methods estimate. Grey line: equal estimates.")}
reference <- estimates |>
  dplyr::filter(method == "lm") |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast, effect_lm = effect)
estimates |>
  dplyr::filter(method != "lm") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(reference, by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(method = factor(method, levels = intensity)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = effect_lm, y = effect)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change, lm", y = "log2 fold change") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r correlation}
correlation <- function(column) {
  wide <- estimates |>
    dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast, method, value = dplyr::all_of(column)) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = value)
  r <- stats::cor(wide[intensity])
  data.frame(
    measure = column,
    method_1 = factor(rownames(r)[row(r)], levels = intensity),
    method_2 = factor(colnames(r)[col(r)], levels = intensity),
    r = as.vector(r)
  )
}
correlations <- dplyr::bind_rows(correlation("effect"), correlation("statistic"))
lowest <- correlations |>
  dplyr::filter(as.integer(method_1) < as.integer(method_2)) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(r, n = 1, by = measure, with_ties = FALSE)
```

The effects agree more closely than the statistics, which also depend on each method's standard error and degrees of freedom. The lowest correlation of the effects is `r sprintf("%.2f", lowest$r[lowest$measure == "effect"])` (`r lowest$method_1[lowest$measure == "effect"]` and `r lowest$method_2[lowest$measure == "effect"]`), that of the statistics `r sprintf("%.2f", lowest$r[lowest$measure == "statistic"])` (`r lowest$method_1[lowest$measure == "statistic"]` and `r lowest$method_2[lowest$measure == "statistic"]`).

```{r correlation_plot, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 12, fig.cap = paste0("Pearson correlation between the intensity methods of the log2 fold changes (effect) and of the statistics, on the ", nrow(shared), " protein and contrast pairs that all of them estimate.")}
ggplot(correlations, aes(x = method_1, y = method_2, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~measure) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166ac") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

# Significant calls

```{r calls}
calls <- aligned |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% intensity) |>
  dplyr::summarise(significant = sum(status %in% c("up", "down")), .by = method)
fewest <- dplyr::slice_min(calls, significant, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
most <- dplyr::slice_max(calls, significant, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

At FDR 0.1 the intensity methods call between `r fewest$significant` (`r fewest$method`) and `r most$significant` (`r most$method`) of the `r n_pairs` pairs significant; the detection models call `r sum(aligned$status[!aligned$method %in% intensity] %in% c("up", "down"))`.

```{r volcano, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 9, fig.cap = "Volcano plots of the intensity methods, both contrasts, coloured by the status at FDR 0.1. Pairs without a p-value are not shown."}
aligned |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% intensity, !is.na(p.value)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    method = factor(method, levels = intensity),
    status = factor(status, levels = names(status_colours))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = effect, y = -log10(p.value), colour = status)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = status_colours) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change", y = "-log10(p-value)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Where the methods contradict each other

`$conflicts()` counts, per pair, the methods in each status and flags three contradictions: `sign_conflict` (up in one method, down in another), `significance_conflict` (significant in one, tested but not significant in another) and `coverage_conflict` (significant in one, not estimated by another). The detection models call no pair significant here, so with them nearly every pair significant in an intensity method would be a significance conflict (`r sum(comparison$conflicts()$significance_conflict)` of `r n_pairs` pairs). The conflicts are therefore counted among the intensity methods only.

```{r conflicts}
intensity_comparison <- ContrastsComparison$new(analyses[intensity], fdr_threshold = 0.1)
conflicts <- intensity_comparison$conflicts()
intensity_aligned <- intensity_comparison$aligned()
conflicts |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_conflict"), sum), pairs = dplyr::n()) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Protein and contrast pairs with each kind of conflict among the intensity methods.")
```

## Opposite signs

```{r sign_conflicts}
sign_rows <- intensity_aligned |>
  dplyr::semi_join(dplyr::filter(conflicts, sign_conflict), by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::filter(status %in% c("up", "down")) |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast, method, effect, FDR, status)
knitr::kable(sign_rows, digits = 3, caption = "Significant calls of the pairs that are up in one method and down in another.")
```

All of these calls have an absolute log2 fold change of at most `r round(max(abs(sign_rows$effect)), 2)`.

## Significant in one method, not in another

```{r significance_conflicts}
intensity_aligned |>
  dplyr::semi_join(dplyr::filter(conflicts, significance_conflict), by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::count(method, status) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(method, intensity)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Status in each method of the ", sum(conflicts$significance_conflict),
    " pairs that are significant in some intensity methods and tested but not significant in others."
  ))
```

## Significant in one method, not estimated by another

```{r coverage_conflicts}
intensity_aligned |>
  dplyr::semi_join(dplyr::filter(conflicts, coverage_conflict), by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::filter(status == "not estimated") |>
  dplyr::count(method, name = "pairs") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pairs significant in some intensity method that a method does not estimate.")
```

Most of them are the single-peptide proteins `lmer_nested` cannot fit; the others are the proteins without observations in a group. The methods that estimate those report:

```{r gap_estimates}
intensity_aligned |>
  dplyr::semi_join(gap, by = c("protein_Id", "contrast")) |>
  dplyr::filter(status != "not estimated") |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast, method, estimate_type, effect, p.value, FDR, status) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Estimates of the pairs lm cannot estimate. estimate_type lod_imputed: the missing group set to the limit of detection.")
```

# Results of another tool

`ContrastsComparison` also takes a `ContrastsTable` holding another tool's results. Its `ContrastConfiguration` names the result columns, so they need not be renamed; only the protein column must match. Here plain limma, as its User's Guide recommends for group comparisons (`~ 0 + group`, `makeContrasts()`, `contrasts.fit()`, `eBayes()`), on the protein intensities:

```{r plain_limma}
wide <- lfq_protein$data_wide(as.matrix = TRUE)
design <- stats::model.matrix(~ 0 + group_, wide$annotation)
contrast_matrix <- limma::makeContrasts(
  A_vs_Ctrl = group_A - group_Ctrl,
  B_vs_Ctrl = group_B - group_Ctrl,
  levels = design
)
fit <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(limma::lmFit(wide$data, design), contrast_matrix))
plain_limma <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(colnames(contrast_matrix), function(name) {
  top <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = name, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  data.frame(protein_Id = rownames(top), comparison = name, top, row.names = NULL)
}))
head(plain_limma, 3)

limma_columns <- ContrastConfiguration$new(
  subject_id = "protein_Id",
  contrast_col = "comparison",
  effect_col = "logFC",
  score_col = "t",
  pvalue_col = "P.Value",
  fdr_col = "adj.P.Val",
  avg_abundance_col = "AveExpr"
)
limma_comparison <- ContrastsComparison$new(
  list(
    plain_limma = ContrastsTable$new(plain_limma, model_name = "plain limma", config = limma_columns),
    limma_unweighted = build_contrast_analysis(lfq_protein, "~ group_", contrasts, method = "limma", weights = NULL),
    limma = analyses$limma
  ),
  fdr_threshold = 0.1
)
knitr::kable(limma_comparison$coverage())
```

```{r limma_differences}
limma_wide <- limma_comparison$aligned() |>
  dplyr::select(protein_Id, contrast, method, effect, p.value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = c(effect, p.value))
limma_conflicts <- limma_comparison$conflicts()
```

Without weights, prolfqua's `limma` reproduces plain limma: the largest difference is `r format(max(abs(limma_wide$effect_limma_unweighted - limma_wide$effect_plain_limma), na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1)` in the effect and `r format(max(abs(limma_wide$p.value_limma_unweighted - limma_wide$p.value_plain_limma), na.rm = TRUE), digits = 1)` in the p-value, and neither estimates the `r nrow(gap)` pairs of proteins without observations in a group (plain limma warns about them and returns NA). By default prolfqua weights each protein intensity by the number of peptides behind it (`nr_children`); this shifts the estimates by up to `r round(max(abs(limma_wide$effect_limma - limma_wide$effect_plain_limma), na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, and `r sum(limma_conflicts$significance_conflict)` pairs are significant with one of the two and not with the other.

# Notes on single methods

`ropecaV2_nested` estimates the correlation of the peptides of a protein from the residuals, here `r round(analyses$ropecaV2_nested$contrast$rho, 2)`, so that proteins with many peptides are not reported as more significant.

`hurdle_nested` joins an intensity model (`lm_impute`) and a detection model (`binomial_firth_nested`) by protein and contrast and combines their p-values with Fisher's method, as msqrob2's hurdle model does. `diff` comes from the intensity model; a protein estimated by one component only keeps that component's p-value. `ContrastsHurdleFacade` builds the same from two fitted analyses:

```{r hurdle}
hurdle <- ContrastsHurdleFacade$new(analyses$lm_impute, analyses$binomial_firth_nested)
hurdle$get_contrasts() |>
  dplyr::count(contrast, hurdle_components, name = "pairs")
```
